newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Any EMU delay bad for markets, economy - Guterres.
newsitem.headline: Any EMU delay bad for markets, economy - Guterres.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said that any delay in implementing the single currency would send a "very negative" signal to financial markets and hurt Europe's economy.
"Any delay...could upset the working of the financial markets and this could have very bad consequences for the European economy as a whole," Guterres told journalists.
He had been asked to comment on market fears that the launch of the single currency, set for January 1999, could be delayed partly because of Germany's difficulties in meeting the deficit goal.

Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher was quoted as saying by the magazine Boerse Online that he doubted that Germany would meet the deficit goal and that, in this case, the only thing to do would be to delay the launch of monetary union.
Guterres reaffirmed his confidence that Portugal would pass the entry tests to become a founder member of the single currency at its launch.
The government predicts a budget deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year, inside the three percent ceiling for participating in economic and monetary union (EMU).
